walkthroughs.body_html:
Inject mouse with antigen → lymphocytes are produced.

Fuse lymphocytes with tumour cells to make hybridomas. They divide forever AND make one specific antibody.

Pregnancy tests, disease diagnosis, targeted cancer treatment, locating clots, separating molecules.

asks you to evaluate — high specificity but cost, side effects, ethics.

Carcinogens (e.g. tobacco), UV radiation and viruses can trigger cancer by mutating DNA.

Preventable risks: smoking, obesity, alcohol, sun. Roughly 4 in 10 cancers linked to lifestyle.

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.

mcqs.q: How do vaccines protect you from a disease?
options: They expose your immune system to a harmless form of the pathogen so memory cells form, allowing rapid response if exposed later.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
Antibodies are tiny knives that physically cut pathogens apart.
Vaccines kill the pathogen if it ever enters the body.

mcqs.q: What makes antibodies effective against pathogens?
options: They have a specific shape complementary to antigens on a particular pathogen, marking it for destruction or neutralising it.
Antibodies are tiny knives that physically cut pathogens apart.
Antibodies are general-purpose proteins that work against any pathogen.
Vaccines provide antibodies for life by adding them directly to the blood.
